ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all identified UBOs, directors, and counterparties against FINTRAC guidance, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, Canadian autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, and the domestic Royal Canadian Mounted Police civil enforcement registry. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) and former PEPs within 12 months of leaving public office. Negative news and adverse-media sweeps are to be refreshed every 180 days, and all screening results must be documented and retained for at least seven years per PCMLTFA record-keeping obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Registry, Service Alberta) via https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use Latin alphabetical characters and may include Arabic numerals. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into English or French. The name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and the legal element 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation'. Only English or French forms are accepted; no local script is otherwise mandated. Hyphens, slashes, commas, periods, and ampersands are permitted subject to registry discretion.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant must file a written administrative review request with the Alberta Corporate Registry (Name Review Committee within Service Alberta) within 30 calendar days of the adverse decision. The request should include the original NUANS report, the rejection letter, and a corrected or alternative name proposal. If the administrative review is denied, the applicant may seek re-hearing or judicial review in the Alberta Court of Queen's Bench pursuant to Alberta Business Corporations Act, s. 227(2). While an appeal is pending, the original name reservation may be held for a single supplementary period, provided that the total reservation does not exceed 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally acceptable for an ISIC 4631 specialty green coffee bean import/distribution ULC, provided the address is a physical street address in Alberta (not a P.O. Box), it is staffed during normal business hours for service of process, and corporate records remain accessible in Alberta as required by Business Corporations Act s. 96. A licensed Alberta registered agent is required where the principals or directors reside outside Canada. The absence of a physical warehouse or retail storefront does not prejudice commercial substance for an import-only trading entity, though commercial banks may require additional economic nexus information during account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. For a non-regulated, normal-risk green coffee import company, the annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by Alberta Corporate Registry or FINTRAC is estimated at under 5%. The probability rises to approximately 10%–15% where filings are incomplete, UBO disclosure is deficient, or an entity/principals appear on a watchlist or adverse-media screening. No industry-specific physical inspection regime exists for ISIC 4631 wholesale coffee distribution.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 10 (name requirements and ULC designation), 12 (incorporation), 15 (contents and legal effect of articles), 17 (filing and certificate of incorporation), 22-23 (registered office and records office) and Part 8 (directors and officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (Government of Alberta), via the Corporate Access online filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (prescribed form under the Business Corporations Act, Alberta) executed by subscribers, together with director consents; the articles expressly omit any limitation on shareholder liability to qualify for the 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' ('ULC') designation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow/trust deposit requirement under the ABCA; shares may be subscribed at nominal value, and only the stated capital account must reflect the consideration received.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscription agreements of the founding shareholders are approved and 10,000 Class A Common Shares without par value are issued to the subscribers at CAD 0.01 per share, for aggregate consideration of CAD 100, receipt acknowledged and credited to stated capital; (2) the registered office of the Corporation is established at its physical address in Calgary, Alberta, and remains accessible for service of process during normal business hours; (3) the following officers are appointed: President, Treasurer and Corporate Secretary, each authorized to execute banking and trade-finance documents; and (4) by-law No. 1 is adopted, and the opening of corporate bank accounts and documentary letter-of-credit facilities for green coffee purchases is authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) through a licensed NUANS search provider; reservation administered via the Corporate Access portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three preferred English names for the specialty green coffee importing ULC through a licensed NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system; confirm the selected name is not confusingly similar to an existing federal or Alberta trademark and that it contains the mandatory 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' designation. Reserve the cleared name for 90 days and retain the search report for the articles filing.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report evidencing no conflicting name
Name reservation receipt or certificate
Trademark clearance memo (CIPO database)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries the name, file secondary name choices within the same reservation window or obtain a written consent/waiver from the conflicting name holder; alternatively adopt a numbered Alberta company name with a 'ULC' suffix.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (articles review desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation under s. 15 ABCA, specifying the ULC name, registered physical office address in Alberta, authorized share structure including Class A Common Shares, number of directors, and no limitation on shareholder liability. Each subscriber and director signs the articles, and each proposed director signs a consent to act. For foreign corporate subscribers, execute a notarized power of attorney authorizing Alberta counsel.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Incorporation (prescribed ABCA form)
Consent to Act as director for each proposed director
Subscriber list with executed share subscription agreement
Notarized power of attorney or board authorization for any corporate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry requires corrections, amend the articles internally and resubmit the corrected signature pages; ministerial errors may be cured by a post-incorporation correction filing without affecting corporate status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing, Certificate of Incorporation and Registry Data Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed articles and pay the applicable filing fee (approximately CAD 275) through the Corporate Access e-filing interface. Once the Registrar validates compliance with s. 17 ABCA, a Certificate of Incorporation is issued and the ULC's legal existence commences. Confirm that the registered office, directors and unlimited liability designation appear on the Corporate Information System (CIS) record.
required_dossiers: Filed Articles of Incorporation and Registrar's payment receipt
Certificate of Incorporation issued under s. 17(2) ABCA
Corporate Registry (CIS) summary confirming active status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is refused or queried, review the Registry's deficiency letter, correct the articles or consents within 30 days and refile; if incorporation is inadvertently defective, the available cure includes a fresh filing or a court declaration under the ABCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number, GST/HST and Trade Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online; CBSA import/export account alignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated ULC with the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) and a corporate income tax account; open a GST/HST account (mandatory once annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, with voluntary registration recommended to recover GST charged on ocean freight and import-related costs). Open an Import/Export (RM) account at the same time for future containerized green coffee clearances through the CBSA single window.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
CRA Business Registration Online confirmation or Form RC1
Alberta Corporate Registry active transcript
List of directors with contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA requests identity verification of directors, submit notarized proof of identification and residential address; if the account is temporarily locked, contact the CRA Business Registration line with the BN and incorporation file number to reactivate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Records Office Designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta); the ULC itself under ss. 22-23 ABCA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Designate a physical, geo-coded registered office in Alberta that is not a post office box and is open during normal business hours for service of process; submit the registered office notice and occupant's consent with the Registry. Maintain a separate records office, which may be counsel's office, holding the articles, by-laws, minutes, register of directors and share register per s. 23.
required_dossiers: Consent of registered office occupant (landlord or corporate agent)
Registered office notice or confirmation form
Lease or evidence of right to occupy the Alberta address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality cannot geo-validate the address, provide the legal land description and civic address certificate; any subsequent change of registered office requires filing a notice of change with the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, By-law Adoption and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the ULC; corporate secretary (internal governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, in person or by unanimous electronic resolution, promptly after the certificate issues. Adopt the First Board Resolution covering share subscription and issuance, registered office adoption, officer appointments and bank signatories; adopt by-law No. 1; approve share certificates and the share register; and resolve the auditor exemption or appointment of an accountant where applicable.
required_dossiers: Notice or waiver of first board meeting
Minutes of first directors' meeting incorporating the pro-forma resolution
By-law No. 1 and executed share certificates
Officer consents and specimen signatures for banking purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer or director declines appointment, the board appoints a qualified alternate and files a notice of director change; if the by-law is queried by the Registry, amend it by a subsequent directors' or shareholders' resolution.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); digital portal: CRA My Business Account and GST/HST NETFILE at www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement (Alberta has no separate tax authority).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Alberta ULC incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) obtains its Business Number (BN), corporate income tax account (RC), GST/HST account (RT) and payroll account (RP) automatically through CRA Corporation Integration upon incorporation. A foreign entity not incorporated in Canada (e.g., a non-resident shareholder establishing a Canadian branch or carrying on commercial activity in Alberta) must apply on Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) with certified incorporation documents, a completed Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) entity information schedule, a copy of the foreign registration certificate, and a non-resident declaration; CRA issues the BN immediately upon verification, and GST/HST registration is effective from the application date. Importing into Canada as a non-resident makes GST/HST registration mandatory even below the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (US federal check-the-box perspective: an Alberta ULC lacks limited liability within Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3 and therefore defaults to a partnership (multi-member) or disregarded entity (single-member), unless Form 8832 elects corporate treatment). For Canadian domestic tax purposes the same ULC is an Entity_Level_Taxation taxpayer — a Part I taxable corporation subject to the 15% federal rate and the 8% Alberta rate (23% combined), and it is the GST/HST registrant of record; the pass-through status is recognized only under foreign tax law and Canada-US Tax Treaty Article IV(7).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) US Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3(c) 'check-the-box' election on IRS Form 8832 must be filed within 75 days of the desired effective date; default pass-through treatment arises without filing. 2) Election under Article IV(7) of the Canada-US Tax Convention: the US shareholder files the prescribed ULC treaty-election statement with the CRA and delivers a copy to the ULC as withholding agent, causing the ULC to be treated as fiscally transparent so that US-resident shareholders obtain reduced Part XIII withholding and treaty benefits. 3) GST/HST voluntary registration election (Excise Tax Act s. 240(3)) allows a small supplier to register early to recover input tax credits. 4) Hybrid mismatch elections and structural elections under Income Tax Act ss. 18.3-18.5 (effective 1 July 2022) do not create a standalone 'check-the-box' for Canadian purposes; taxpayers neutralize mismatches by fixing the entity's foreign classification or contractual allocations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Excise Tax Act, Part IX; Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax (PST) or HST, so the single indirect tax is the 5% federal GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148(1), measured on worldwide taxable supplies over the preceding four calendar quarters; registration becomes mandatory on the transaction that exceeds the threshold. Non-resident importers must register (or self-assess at the border) even below CAD 30,000. Green coffee beans are zero-rated as basic groceries (Schedule VI, Part III), so the effective rate on the wholesale supply and on export sales is 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no tax-authority e-invoice stamping, and no API integration with the CRA for transaction-level invoicing in Canada. The CRA requires records to be retained in machine-readable form (ETA s. 286; Income Tax Act s. 230), accepts EDI/X12 and Peppol (Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Framework) on a voluntary basis, and mandates electronic filing of GST/HST returns (GST/HST NETFILE) for registrants with annual gross revenue exceeding CAD 1.5 million; paper filing remains available below that threshold. The GST/HST return (GST34) must be filed and the net tax remitted within one month after the end of the reporting period (monthly or quarterly), or within three months for annual filers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Two independent zero-rating bases apply to the specialty green coffee bean trade: (a) domestic zero-rating as basic groceries for human consumption under ETA Schedule VI, Part III (0% GST, full ITC entitlement); and (b) export zero-rating under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 5 (goods shipped by the supplier to a destination outside Canada) and s. 6 (goods delivered to a non-resident recipient for export in the course of the recipient's business). Offshore services (e.g., storage, freight management) are zero-rated under Part V, s. 7 if performed wholly outside Canada. The registrant must prove actual export by retaining contemporaneous shipping and payment evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Commercial Invoice (vendor's invoice stating exporter, consignee, container number, INCOTERM, quantity, unit price in USD/CAD, and commodity HS code — e.g., HS 0901.11 for green arabica coffee)
Electronic B13A Export Declaration / Canadian Export Reporting System (ERS) filing confirmation for goods valued over CAD 2,000
Bill of Lading (ocean/air waybill) evidencing foreign destination and the shipper-of-record
Container seal number and Customs transit/export documentation or the ERS 'Released' acknowledgment

Payment and FX settlement proof: SWIFT MT103 inbound remittance credit advice, documentary Letter of Credit settlement advice, or bank transfer confirmation (the functional equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate, which Canada does not issue)
Warehouse/receipt records and the purchase import documentation (Form B3 or EDI/ACI e-manifest) for traceability back to the originating export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess within four years from the end of the reporting period (ETA s. 298) and longer in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or waiver. If the export documents do not establish physical export, CRA re-taxes the supply at 5% GST and disallows related input tax credits with arrears interest (s. 280). Gross negligence penalty: 50% of the net tax amount; false statements/omissions (s. 285): fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment up to 12 months on summary conviction; tax evasion (ETA s. 327): penalties up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to five years. Records must be retained for six years from the last day of the period to which they relate; failure to produce export documentation shifts the burden to the registrant and triggers immediate clawback with interest. Export zero-rating claims are scrutinized via the CRA 'Exports and Trade' verification program when bill-to/ship-to addresses differ, when the goods return to Canada, or when settlement of the export invoice is not received within 180 days of the bill of lading date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary, lender-of-last-resort and large-value settlement authority; foreign-exchange policy is administered under the Currency Act and Bank of Canada Act, while FINTRAC supervises AML/CFT and money-services-business registration under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current- and capital-account convertibility (IMF Article VIII) and imposes no exchange-control approval for inward or outward remittances. Green coffee import payments and profits can be freely settled in CAD/USD; however, an Alberta ULC's distributions to non-resident shareholders may attract Part XIII withholding tax (reduced under the Canada-US treaty to 5 per cent for qualifying corporate shareholders and 15 per cent for interest as applicable), so equity injections are preferable during capitalization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio; receipts from any re-export of green coffee may be retained indefinitely in USD or foreign-currency accounts. Reporting obligations are limited to CBSA export declarations, FINTRAC large-transaction reporting for CAD 10,000 or more, and CRS/FATCA account disclosures; no central-bank repatriation filing is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: RBC Royal Bank (Royal Bank of Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow account and operational CAD/USD clearing accounts
Operational CAD/USD accounts, SWIFT MT103 hub and trade-finance desk
Operational account with commercial Letter of Credit issuing capacity
Operational account and documentary collection services
Provincial operational and liquidity depository account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Canada has no distinct EMI licence; foreign digital EMIs operated by licensed MSBs/FMSBs registered with FINTRAC can provide low-value supplier disbursements and cross-border FX conversion, but they are not direct participant banks in Payments Canada Lynx and their deposits lack CDIC coverage. For the Alberta ULC's trade-liquidity concentration, documentary credit issuance and regulatory clearability, Schedule I bank accounts remain the only fully viable clearing core.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted for Alberta-incorporated ULCs: FINTRAC allows video verification with notarized government-issued identification and a Certificate of Incumbency/board resolution. However, banks typically require an in-person visit of the ultimate beneficial owner or an authorized director at a Calgary or Edmonton branch when non-resident ownership or complex ULC cross-border tax structures trigger enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legal-form anomaly: an Unlimited Liability Corporation with no minimum capital and unlimited shareholder liability is screened as a potentially opaque or tax-driven structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; articles and unanimous shareholder agreement; Alberta Corporate Registry search; FINTRAC-compliant UBO declaration (25 per cent threshold); legal opinion from Canadian counsel explaining the ULC structure; notarized and apostilled identity documents for all signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident parent ownership chain connected to a higher-risk coffee-origin jurisdiction triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residence certificates and CRS self-certifications for all beneficial owners; corporate organigram with exact shareholding percentages; source-of-wealth statements; bank references from the parent's home institution; registered green-coffee purchase contracts and pro-forma invoices evidencing commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent, similarly sized inbound/outbound wire payments for green coffee matching trade-based money laundering red flags and FINTRAC large-transaction reports.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro-forma and final commercial invoices reconciled to SWIFT MT103 narratives; bills of lading, certificates of origin and phytosanitary certificates per shipment; weight/grade certificates; ICO-compliant sourcing paperwork; documented trade-flow map from origin port to Alberta warehouse.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through or US check-the-box classification of the ULC creating FATCA/CRS mismatches, treaty-shopping suspicion or unusual withholding-tax elections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IRS entity-classification (check-the-box) election and W-8BEN-E/W-9 forms; Canadian and US tax opinions; audited financial statements; board minutes documenting the commercial purpose of the ULC; Part XIII withholding analysis and dividend/interest repatriation plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound shareholder equity by SWIFT MT103 to the ULC's operational CAD/USD account with narrative 'Capital Subscription - Equity Injection for Green Coffee Trading'; no central-bank approval is required in Canada, but the receiving bank will record source-of-funds and file a FINTRAC large-transaction report if the amount equals or exceeds CAD 10,000 equivalent. Prefund the commercial Letter of Credit treasury line through an equity-escrow account to avoid Part XIII withholding on intercompany debt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Pay green-coffee exporters via SWIFT MT103 for open-account and advance-payment shipments; for high-value containerised transactions issue irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit under UCP 600 (MT700) confirmed by the exporter's bank. CAD balances clear through Payments Canada Lynx or ACSS, while USD payments are routed via the Canadian bank's US correspondent (CHIPS/Fedwire) with MT103 series 202/203 status-matching for trade reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards up to 12 months under ISDA 2002 or Canadian Master Agreement treasury lines
CAD/USD FX swaps for short-term liquidity and import-payment matching
Cross-currency swaps between CAD and USD to hedge Letter of Credit financing liabilities
USD/CAD FX European options and zero-cost collars where the bank's credit approval permits
Offshore CAD NDFs are not practical because the Canadian dollar is freely convertible and all hedges are executed onshore as deliverable contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month after the corporation's anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The prescribed filing fee and registry-agent service charges apply. Persistent non-filing may result in administrative dissolution, generally after failure to file for two consecutive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due six months after the end of each taxation year; any corporate balance is generally payable two months after year-end, subject to applicable small-business corporation rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, arrears interest, instalment interest, reassessment exposure, and collection action may apply. The filing does not itself trigger corporate strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general Alberta revenue, asset, or employee threshold automatically requires an audit for a private Alberta corporation. An audit may be required by the articles, a shareholder agreement, financing terms, or shareholder rights. A non-reporting issuer may generally waive appointment of an auditor by the required shareholder resolution under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) are generally applicable. IFRS may be used where elected or required by the corporation's reporting circumstances. Tax computations remain governed by Canadian federal income-tax legislation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not generally require a standalone annual UBO filing with the Corporate Registry for a private Alberta corporation. The corporation should maintain current ownership and control information, document changes promptly, and provide beneficial ownership information to competent authorities, financial institutions, and regulated reporting entities when legally required. Share transfers must be recorded in the securities or share register and supported by appropriate transfer documentation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Securities and Share Transfers
Minute Book containing shareholder and director resolutions and meeting minutes
Articles, certificates, shareholder agreements, and other corporate records required by the Alberta Business Corporations Act

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 225-600 per year, excluding filing fees, tax services, mail forwarding, and extraordinary corporate actions.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,500-10,000 for a small private corporation if an audit is required; no statutory audit fee applies where a valid exemption or waiver is available.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) on first CAD 500,000 of active business income at reduced combined rate of 11% (Federal 9% + Alberta 2%); Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Investment Tax Credits (ITCs) up to 35% refundable for qualifying expenditures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically via CRA's e-file (e.g., through certified tax software) or via TELEFILE for eligible corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, deadline is June 30 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue (gross sales, service revenue, and other income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide revenue; if the ULC is a non-resident corporation, report only Canadian-source business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net of deductions, capital cost allowance, and loss carryforwards)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxable income attributable to Canadian operations; apply treaty provisions if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax payable (before provincial allocation and credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate federal tax at 15% on taxable income; for non-residents, only Canadian-source income is taxed.
Allocate income to Alberta based on permanent establishment; apply Alberta rate of 8%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance owing plus 1% per full month (up to 12 months) for returns filed after the deadline; repeated failure penalty of 10% for second offense; interest on unpaid amounts at prescribed rates (currently 8% for corporations).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII tax on dividends paid to non-residents)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a tax treaty, the non-resident recipient must provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from their home tax authority. The Canadian payer must file Form NR301 (or NR302 for treaty-based reductions) with the CRA, and the recipient must complete Form NR303 (or NR304) to certify eligibility. For Canada-US treaty, the rate is 5% for corporate shareholders owning at least 10% of voting shares, otherwise 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for royalties and 25% for interest (subject to exceptions for arm's length interest). Treaty rates: Canada-US treaty reduces royalties to 10% (for copyrights, patents, etc.) and interest to 15% (or 0% for arm's length interest paid to a US resident). Other treaties may vary.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for services; CAD 5 million for tangible goods, intangible property, and interest transactions with non-residents (per CRA's contemporaneous documentation requirements).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in Canada, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) applies to disallow transactions lacking genuine economic substance. The CRA may recharacterize transactions if the main purpose is tax avoidance. For ULCs, the unlimited liability structure may be scrutinized for treaty shopping; substance must be demonstrated through real business activities, employees, and premises in Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or misrepresentation of cross-border transactions to reduce tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act (s. 239): fine of 50% to 200% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years, and civil penalties of 50% of the understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes (s. 227.1) if they fail to withhold or remit; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a conduit with no real business activity, employees, or assets in Canada; using the ULC solely to access treaty benefits or defer tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment disallowing tax benefits, plus penalties of 25% of the tax benefit (s. 163.2); potential treaty override and denial of treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be assessed for penalties if they authorized or acquiesced to the sham arrangement; personal liability for tax benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to report large cash transactions (over CAD 10,000) or suspicious transactions to FINTRAC; inadequate KYC procedures for coffee import payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1 million for corporations; criminal charges for money laundering under the Criminal Code (s. 462.31) with imprisonment up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined up to CAD 500,000 for AML violations; travel bans and imprisonment for willful blindness.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing on coffee bean purchases from related foreign suppliers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may adjust prices, impose penalties of 10% of the net adjustment (s. 247(3)), plus interest; double taxation risk if not corrected.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly participated in the transfer pricing mispricing; personal liability for unpaid penalties.
